description: Which file of a model to download for a machine. Every GGUF quantization the repo publishes is read from its file listing (sizes measured, split files summed), the memory each needs at your context length is computed, and the answer names the largest file that runs on the machine with room (pick), a larger one that only barely fits (stretch), when nothing runs at that context the file that runs at the longest shorter one (atShorterContext), and for every file its verdict, its bits per weight and the longest context it still runs at. Works for a tracked model (model, a slug) and for any public Hugging Face repo (repo). The machine is a hardware id, several identical cards (count), or a free memory figure (memory_gb). Files are ranked by size only: a larger file keeps more bits per weight; there is no quality rating and no speed figure. When the model's shape cannot be read every verdict is UNKNOWN and only the sizes are given. Limits as for measure_model: 20 calls per hour per caller; a reading is reused for 24 hours.

context.description: Context length in tokens (default 8192); capped at the model's own window.

count.description: How many identical graphics cards (default 1). Their memory adds up; the answer says what that assumes.

hardware.description: Hardware id, e.g. rtx-3060-12gb. Ids come from list_hardware. Leave it out when you pass memory_gb.

memory_gb.description: For a machine that is not on the list, instead of hardware: the memory of one graphics card, or of the Mac, in GB.

model.description: A tracked model by slug, e.g. qwen3-8b. Slugs come from trending_models. Pass this or repo, not both.

ram_gb.description: System RAM behind the card(s), for what spills over (default 32).

repo.description: Any public Hugging Face repo as "owner/name" (a GGUF repo, or an original whose most downloaded GGUF build is then used), or its huggingface.co link.

type.description: What memory_gb describes: "gpu" (default, a plug-in card) or "mac" (unified memory).

name: best_quant
title: Best quantization for a machine
